# Supplementary methods and results

## Reproducibility map

The repository treats manuscript prose as a view over frozen machine-readable
artifacts. The principal claims can be recomputed from the following experiment
directories.

| Claim | Experiment artifact |
|---|---|
| Six-cell S1 split | `experiments/s1_article_factorial/results/` |
| S1 planning-feature audit | `experiments/s1_planning_feature_audit/results/audit.json` |
| Replay and rescue | `experiments/s1_replay_rescue/results/` |
| Decoder boundary and precision | `experiments/boundary_precision_policy/results/` |
| Private residual references | `experiments/natural_residual_carrier_regimes/results/` and `experiments/cross_scale_normalized_residual/results/` |
| Neutral synonym routing | `experiments/neutral_synonym_repair/results/` |
| Matched semantic-triad routing | `experiments/matched_semantic_triads_repaired/results/` |
| Independent Figure 4 recomputation | `experiments/neutral_synonym_repair/results/independent_recomputation.json` |
| Closed-loop gain | `experiments/closed_loop_gain_law/results/` |
| Sparse 1B stress tests | `experiments/gemma_1b_effect_matched/results/` and `experiments/gemma_1b_sparse_frontier/results/` |

All summary JSON files record model identifiers, sample sizes, interval methods,
and primary settings. Plotting scripts read those artifacts rather than values
copied from manuscript prose. The 270M model snapshot is
`9b0cfec892e2bc2afd938c98eabe4e4a7b1e0ca1`; the affine Gemma Scope 2
dictionary snapshot is `b218cd5d69dc2fa71cff448b68d625e6c9702d49` with configuration
`width_262k_l0_medium_affine`. Discussed decoder/encoder vectors and selection
metadata are archived under `experiments/archived_feature_vectors/`.

The frozen S1 audit checks its relationship to the planning-feature motivation
without rerunning inference. Each of the four selected features is active at the
pre-article position and has positive direct attribution to the intended future
noun on all eight selection prompts. Together with the intervention results,
this establishes future-noun-attributed pre-article causal handles. It does not
establish noun-specific semantic identity: the same
features recur across distinct future nouns, and S1 selection jointly required
positive article attribution. We therefore retain the term
*attribution-selected S1 features* rather than claiming an independently
selected Hanna-style semantic planning feature.

## Exact six-cell measurements

For each fixed article, the intervention remains active at its original
pre-article position during noun prediction. This differs from deleting the
intervention after the article is inserted. We compute full-sequence forwards
with `use_cache=False`; multi-token noun likelihoods are teacher-forced one token
at a time. Full-vocabulary TV is
\(TV(p,q)=\frac12\sum_v|p_v-q_v|\). We additionally record Jensen--Shannon
divergence, top-\(k\) overlap, target-minus-source logits for prespecified lexical
twins, vector cosine, and
\(\|E_{\rm total}-E_{\rm public}-E_{\rm private}\|_1\).

The S1 decomposition over all 20 held-out prompts is:

| Quantity | Mean | 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total noun TV | 0.893 | [0.784, 0.969] |
| Treated-token replay TV | 0.891 | [0.776, 0.969] |
| Matched treated-token leftover TV | 0.028 | [0.021, 0.035] |
| Replay--total cosine | 0.950 | [0.903, 0.979] |

Nineteen prompts switch article and noun. On that descriptive switched subset,
total, replay, and leftover TVs are 0.940, 0.937, and 0.029. We use the all-prompt
values in the headline to avoid post-selection.

## Boundary and stochastic-policy audits

Native model, CLT, and residual tensors are bfloat16. A diagnostic head casts
the final normalized residual and unembedding to float32 without rerunning the
transformer in float32. Across three prespecified prompts, a search of width
\(2.44\times10^{-4}\) still produces 0.992 free-path TV while fixed `a` and
`an` move 0.009 and 0.004. The audit shows that native 0/0.125-logit steps reflect
final-readout quantization, while the continuation discontinuity under greedy
article choice is real.

For stochastic policies we renormalize over `a/an` and mix the two fixed-article
noun distributions. Retained article mass exceeds 0.998 at low temperature in
the boundary assay. Policy-vector alignment with the total remains at least
0.99 across tested temperatures; the private component remains small. These
calculations evaluate the exact conditional mixture and introduce no sampling
variance. The strength-boundary and temperature sweeps make the same point
visually: the total effect tracks the public component while the fixed-token
leftover stays small (@fig-app-boundary).

![S1 boundary and stochastic-policy robustness. A: a float32 final-head audit resolves the article margin more finely around the boundary. B: softening the article policy turns the discrete switch into graded probability movement. C: total influence shrinks with temperature, with the public component tracking it and the fixed-token residual remaining small.](manuscript/figures/fig_boundary_precision_policy.png){#fig-app-boundary width=95%}

## Private-route controls and scale

Natural-state-derived patches are constructed from target-uncued descriptions.
The pooled development sweep selects decoder layer 12 at 270M and layer 14 at
1B. At each scale and route condition we report raw target-minus-source movement,
fraction of the baseline lexical gap closed, target-odds multiplier, patch norm
relative to natural residual RMS, and stochastic public/private TVs. Controls
include a semantic wrong target and sign reversal. The target effect is positive
at both scales, while normalized comparisons do not support a monotone increase
at 1B. The fuller normalized comparison in @fig-app-private-scale shows both the
cross-scale replication and the absence of a monotone scale trend; the control
directions remain much weaker than the intended target direction.

![Full cross-scale private-route comparison. A: development layer profiles. B: normalized target efficacy across patch strengths. C--D: public and fixed-token effect magnitudes across strength. The target effect is present at both Gemma 3 270M and 1B, but normalization does not support a monotone increase with scale. Specificity controls appear in @fig-private.](manuscript/figures/fig_cross_scale_normalized_residual.png){#fig-app-private-scale width=95%}

The stronger dense residual reference patches the decoder-layer output at the
inserted article position. Four development pairs select layer 12; four held-out
same-article pairs yield 6.44 target-specific logits versus 0.14 for ten
matched-norm random directions. This is a reachability and stack-sensitivity
control, not evidence that S1 represents the same lexical direction.

## Neutral synonym assay details

The bare neutral template ending immediately after the definition failed
mediator-support screening before route inference:
`called` frequently outranked both articles, mean `a/an` mass was approximately
0.27, and only 7/14 prompts had an article top token. The frozen evaluated format
therefore uses one unrelated demonstration:

> Someone who studies living organisms is a biologist. [definition] is

Donor prompts append `Use exactly the word [word]` to the same format. The
demonstration names neither tested synonym, initial letter, nor tested article
class. Leave-one-family-out development selection chooses layer 17 in all folds.
All 14 directions have positive local efficacy on the neutral evaluated prompt,
despite direct donor separation being positive in 13/14.

At \(s=1,\tau=1\), the main route quantities are:

| Regime | Public TV | Private TV | Public target effect | Private target effect |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Between article classes (N=6) | 0.176 | 0.021 | 0.189 | 0.019 |
| Within `a` class (N=8) | 0.009 | 0.061 | -0.001 | 0.093 |

Both signed simple effects have the predicted direction under exact sign flips,
and the independent family-label interaction has exact two-sided
\(p=0.00033\) over 3,003 assignments. The interaction remains positive for all
12 strength-temperature settings (@fig-app-synonym-robustness). This visual
check shows that the sign reversal is not peculiar to one chosen strength or
article-policy temperature. We archive the rejected bare-neutral output
under `results_bare_neutral_invalid_support/` rather than silently replacing it.

The repaired paired extension freezes 22 candidate semantic triads before
screening. Fourteen pass the route-blind tokenization, local-efficacy, and
article-support criteria. Each retained definition is evaluated from the same
source word and neutral prompt with one same-article and one cross-article
target. At \(s=1,\tau=1\), within-class \(R=P-H\) is
\(-0.032\ [-0.057,-0.010]\), cross-class \(R\) is
\(0.087\ [0.046,0.132]\), and their paired difference is
\(0.120\ [0.077,0.161]\). Thirteen of 14 paired shifts are positive (one-sided
sign test \(p=0.00092\); exact magnitude-sensitive sign-randomization
\(p=0.000122\)); eight have the strict double-dissociation
sign. The paired interaction remains positive at every combination of three
strengths and four temperatures. This is the primary control for semantic-family
composition in the mediator-relative claim.

The outcome-blind potency audit does not find stronger cross-article
interventions. Mean cross versus within direction norms are 699 versus 761
(paired difference \(-62\ [-188,60]\)); fixed-article local efficacies are
0.353 versus 0.415 (difference \(-0.063\ [-0.174,0.063]\)); and treated article
support is 0.912 versus 0.913. Cross targets do have a higher baseline
target-minus-source lexical gap (paired difference 7.01 logits), so target-word
identity is not held fixed; this is disclosed rather than interpreted as route
evidence. Because neither direction norm nor fixed-mediator causal potency
favors the cross arm, no outcome-blind efficacy rescaling is triggered.

Semantic validity was assessed during pre-model curation before this candidate
set was frozen and before tokenization, model screening, or route computation.

An independent, artifact-only recomputation imports none of the experiment's
analysis or plotting code. Starting from frozen row-level outputs, it reproduces
all 14 local-efficacy checks, article-support statistics, per-family route
effects, 6/6 and 8/8 original signs, bootstrap summaries, exact sign-flip tests,
the 0.264 independent-group interaction, and its exact \(p=0.00033\) label
permutation test. The same independent runner also reconstructs all 22 triad
eligibility decisions, the exact retained set, every paired route contrast,
both headline tests, and all 12 robustness settings. It fails if any recomputed
headline differs from the frozen summary beyond \(10^{-12}\).

## Closed-loop gain validation

![Closed-loop gain and held-out prediction at Gemma 3 270M. A: attribution is calibrated to local causal pressure, then composed with decoder susceptibility and continuation leverage. B: the composition captures the high-gain regime; orange cells have both observed and predicted article-policy movement above 0.9, while the inset resolves the low-effect cloud. Holdout excludes feature and prompt identity from causal-pressure calibration; intervention-off decoder susceptibility and branch leverage of the held-out prompt are permitted observed inputs. Aggregate R2 is tail-sensitive and is not a claim of uniformly precise cell-level prediction.](manuscript/figures/fig_attribution_channel_calibration.png){#fig-gain width=92%}

The two-branch identity holds to numerical precision. Prediction fits a mapping
from attribution to local article-margin movement on training features and
prompts, then evaluates public TV after composition with intervention-off
susceptibility and branch leverage. Combined feature-and-prompt holdout results
for 270M are:

| Temperature | Attribution only \(R^2\) | + susceptibility | Full composition |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.10 | -0.547 | 0.827 | 0.840 |
| 0.25 | -0.529 | 0.861 | 0.875 |
| 0.50 | -0.191 | 0.857 | 0.870 |
| 1.00 | 0.395 | 0.851 | 0.864 |

At \(\tau=0.1\), constant, susceptibility-only, leverage-only, and activation
baselines have \(R^2=-0.052,-0.082,-0.053,-0.045\). The measured-margin/full-
leverage calculation has \(R^2=1\) by identity and is not a prediction. At 1B,
combined-holdout transfer is weak; we report that failure rather than pool
scales. @fig-app-gain shows the complete diagnostic set: attribution has
moderate local calibration (A), fixed-token attribution correlations are
inconclusive (B), the full 270M composition outperforms simple baselines (C),
bin means expose calibration across the dynamic range (D), tail removal exposes
the aggregate \(R^2\)'s dependence on large effects (E), and temperature and
scale checks delimit transfer (F).

The calibration intervals in panel D use 10,000 crossed bootstrap resamples:
feature and prompt identities are sampled independently with replacement and
their multiplicities are crossed into cell weights. The same blocked procedure
gives aggregate \(R^2=0.840\ [-0.293,0.986]\) and MAE
\(0.0178\ [0.0036,0.0377]\). Panel E reports MAE alongside tail-trimmed
\(R^2\): removing large effects shrinks absolute error but collapses outcome
variance even faster, making \(R^2\) strongly negative without implying large
absolute mistakes.

![Closed-loop gain diagnostics. A: attribution-to-local-efficacy calibration. B: fixed-token target correlations with broad intervals. C: predictive baselines. D: equal-count predicted-versus-observed calibration with crossed feature--prompt bootstrap intervals. E: R2 and MAE respond differently when the largest observed effects are excluded because the remaining outcome variance is tiny. F: temperature robustness at 270M and weak transfer for available 1B handles.](manuscript/figures/fig_gain_diagnostics_appendix.png){#fig-app-gain width=98%}

## Sparse 1B ladder failures

| Sparse handle | Local efficacy | `a/an` support | What follows? |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Frozen top four | No: 0.075-logit mean movement | Yes | No route claim |
| Effect-matched 24 | Yes | No: `called` often dominates | No binary route claim |
| Constrained frontier | Yes | Yes: 20/20 prompts | Low-amplitude hybrid route |

The original four-feature sparse intervention was independently selected from
1,200-node attribution graphs but moved the held-out article margin only 0.075
logits. A 24-feature effect-matched coalition increased local movement but made
non-article tokens such as `called` dominate, invalidating the binary mediator
estimand. A constrained frontier feature at layer 18, feature 5015, preserved
article support on 20/20 prompts. At \(7.5\times\) it changed only one greedy
article, but its exact stochastic decomposition showed low-amplitude hybrid
influence. Reconstruction audits reveal uneven CLT fidelity and a substantial
affine-skip contribution; graph-cap audits make simple truncation a less likely
sole explanation. These results motivate the ladder but do not establish a
scale-dependent reorganization.

## Negative and superseded studies

S2 frequently leaves the intended article domain and is retained only as a
forensic warning. A sparse layer-5 feature produces exploratory fixed-token
movement but has weak matched controls and may encode vowel class. The released
`is/are` subtraction task fails behavioral and local-efficacy prerequisites in
both models, so it cannot test mediator capacity. Earlier first-letter synonym
prompts are superseded because the evaluated source cue contradicted the target
synonym. An arbitrary A/B few-shot pilot does show that context can alter target
nouns with the code fixed (effects 0.224--0.245 across reliability banks), but
the visible context itself remains available and the task is less mechanistically
clean than the neutral synonym assay; it is not part of the main argument.

## NeurIPS checklist notes

The study uses public pretrained models and synthetic prompts. No personal data,
human subjects, or newly collected sensitive data are involved. Compute was run
locally on Apple silicon. Code, frozen configurations, checkpoints, invalidated
outputs, and machine-readable summaries accompany the submission. Confidence
intervals, exact tests, sample sizes, development/evaluation separation, and
known post-selection are stated with each claim.
